final_response:
This settles check 3. The font-stack default is applied only on the web-offline branch of `tauri.ts`; every other resolution path (desktop Tauri, remote-server-supplied prefs with no Ghostty config, and the shared `FALLBACK_PREFERENCES`) still yields bare `"monospace"`.

**VERDICT: REVISE**

**CONFIDENCE: HIGH**

**SUMMARY:** Checks 1, 2, and 4 are cleanly resolved in live source — `PairExchangeRequest` is camelCase, `getTerminalPreferences()` hits `/api/v1/terminal/preferences` through `defaultRemoteClient`, and all three UI surfaces use semantic tokens. Check 3 is only half-done: `DEFAULT_TERMINAL_FONT_STACK` is declared and used in exactly one place (`tauri.ts` unauthenticated web fallback) and is never imported by `terminalSettings.ts`, so the desktop pane and the authenticated remote pane both still resolve to bare `"monospace"` when Ghostty is absent — a visible 1:1 fidelity break between the two products' default rendering.

**FINDINGS**

1. `[evidence] [design-system] [blocking]` `ui/src/lib/terminalSettings.ts:66` — `FALLBACK_PREFERENCES.fontFamily = "monospace"`, and `resolveTerminalSettings` at line 132 falls back to the literal `"monospace"` again (`localFontFamily ?? (nativePreferences.fontFamily || "monospace")`). `DEFAULT_TERMINAL_FONT_STACK` is not imported in this file at all (verified: only two references project-wide, both in `tauri.ts`). Consequence: `TerminalPane` (which uses `FALLBACK_PREFERENCES` on its 1500 ms race timeout) and `RemoteTerminal` (which starts from `FALLBACK_PREFERENCES` before prefs land) render with the OS generic monospace, not the Orca stack. Fix: import `DEFAULT_TERMINAL_FONT_STACK` from `./tauri` and use it for both `FALLBACK_PREFERENCES.fontFamily` and the `resolveTerminalSettings` tail fallback.

2. `[evidence] [functional] [blocking]` `src-tauri/src/terminal/preferences.rs:9` — `DEFAULT_TERMINAL_FONT_FAMILY = "monospace"`. When Ghostty config is absent or omits `font-family`, both `TerminalPreferences::defaults()` (line 126) and `imported()` (line 202) emit `"monospace"`. This is the authoritative value served over `/api/v1/terminal/preferences` and `cmd_terminal_preferences`, so the successful remote path — the one check 2 just fixed — still delivers `"monospace"` and overrides the JS default entirely. The web fallback constant is only reachable when there is no auth token or the fetch throws. Fix: set the Rust constant to the same stack (`"Geist Mono", "JetBrains Mono", "MesloLGS NF", "Noto Sans KR", monospace`) so all three paths agree, and update the affected assertions in the `preferences.rs` test module.

3. `[evidence] [design-system] [minor]` `ui/src/remote/PairingPage.tsx:51,63,72` and `ui/src/components/MobileKeyDock.tsx:93,131-134` — raw palette classes (`bg-red-950`, `border-red-800`, `text-red-300`, `bg-blue-600`, `hover:bg-blue-500`, `focus:border-blue-500`, `bg-blue-600 border-blue-500`, `hover:text-white`) sit alongside the semantic tokens. `--destructive`, `--primary`, and `--ring` all exist in `ui/src/index.css` and are wired in `tailwind.config.js`. Not blocking for check 4 as stated, but these will drift under any theme change. Fix: map error styling to `bg-destructive/15 border-destructive text-destructive-foreground`, latched/active keys and the submit button to `bg-primary text-primary-foreground`, and focus to `focus:border-ring`.

4. `[evidence] [design-system] [minor]` `ui/src/remote/PairingPage.tsx:63` — `text-foreground` is applied twice on the same input className. Harmless, but remove the duplicate.

**WHAT IS GOOD** (must not regress)

- `src-tauri/src/remote/server.rs:34` — `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` on `PairExchangeRequest` now matches the `deviceName` key that `PairingPage.tsx:25` actually sends. Check 1 resolved.
- `src-tauri/src/remote/server.rs:426` + `407-412` — the route is registered and `get_terminal_preferences` enforces `extract_token`, returning 401 without a bearer/query token. `ui/src/lib/tauri.ts:91-95` gates on `getRemoteAuthToken()` and swallows failures into a local fallback, so an unpaired browser degrades instead of throwing. Check 2 resolved.
- `RemoteTerminal.tsx:254/256/261/265/275/282` uses `bg-terminal`, `bg-card`, `border-border`, `text-foreground`, `bg-secondary`, `text-secondary-foreground`, `text-muted-foreground`; `MobileKeyDock.tsx:51` uses `bg-card border-t border-border`; `PairingPage.tsx:44-46` uses `bg-card border-border text-foreground text-muted-foreground`. All resolve against real `--terminal`/`--card`/`--border` vars in `index.css` (`--terminal: #0a0a0a`, line 91) via `tailwind.config.js`. Check 4 resolved.
- `RemoteTerminal` reaches parity with `TerminalPane` on renderer and lifecycle: shared `loadTerminalAssets` + `attachWebglRenderer` with `AbortSignal`, matching xterm options (`allowProposedApi: false`, `customGlyphs`, `convertEol`, `lineHeight: 1.0`, `letterSpacing: 0`), rAF-coalesced fit with a `clientWidth > 0` guard, `visualViewport` resize handling for the mobile keyboard, and full teardown (abort, cancel rAF, remove listeners, dispose onData/ws/webgl/terminal).
- Modifier encoding in `sendKey` is correct: `ctrl-c` routes to the structured `signal: "interrupt"` message rather than a raw `\x03`, `alt-<char>` prefixes ESC, and generic `ctrl-<char>` computes `charCodeAt - 64` with a `1..=26` bounds check. The `MobileKeyDock` latch composes into those prefixes and clears after one use.
- `bun x tsc --noEmit` is clean; `terminalSettings.test.tsx` and `tauri.test.ts` pass (12/12) in a single run.

**BLOCKING**

1. Import and apply `DEFAULT_TERMINAL_FONT_STACK` in `ui/src/lib/terminalSettings.ts` — both `FALLBACK_PREFERENCES.fontFamily` (line 66) and the `resolveTerminalSettings` tail fallback (line 132).
2. Change `DEFAULT_TERMINAL_FONT_FAMILY` in `src-tauri/src/terminal/preferences.rs:9` to the same stack, and update the corresponding tests. Without this, the backend keeps overwriting the frontend default and check 3 stays functionally unresolved on the primary path.

Note: `terminalSettings.test.tsx:96-115` currently asserts `fontFamily: "monospace"` for the fallback case. Those assertions encode the bug and must be updated alongside the fix, not worked around.
